title: Robin Fremel:
headline: The staffer who was there at the start: Adopt-A-Block began in 2020 when the shelves went bare, and six years on she still sees the same families, their kids now grown.
story: Robin Fremel has been on staff at the Dream Center for six years. On the 10 Oct Adopt-A-Block, Kalindi filmed her in the parking lot with the tent and the pallets behind her. Her story is the origin story nobody else on the day tells: Adopt-A-Block started in 2020, in response to COVID, when schools shut and grocery stores were bare. It was the first ministry the Dream Center ever launched. Then the long view: families who have been with them since the beginning, their kids growing up and finding jobs.

Series: Why We're Here. Hopeful, never somber. The hard part (bare shelves, no next meal) is one line each and the cut moves to people coming together and joy. One voice, hers. Kalindi's questions are cut out.

Loops: L1 “Why did a church start a grocery line?” opens 0:00 and closes at 0:06 (schools shut, shelves bare). L2 “What keeps her here six years later?” opens 0:00 and closes in the button (joy spark). Stakes: families who did not know where the next meal came from. They still come, and now they serve.
